root_cause.text: The hp-bioscfg GET_INSTANCE_ID macro performed unsafe sysfs instance lookup by iterating one past the end of type##_data and dereferencing attr_name_kobj->name without verifying attr_name_kobj was non-NULL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for (i = 0; i <= bioscfg_drv.type##_instances_count; i++)` to `for (i = 0; i < bioscfg_drv.type##_instances_count; i++)` and adds `bioscfg_drv.type##_data[i].attr_name_kobj &&` before `strcmp(...attr_name_kobj->name)`, while the CVE/commit explicitly states the original code caused out-of-bounds access and a NULL pointer dereference leading to a kernel panic in `min_length_show()`.

intent_record.what: The loop bound in the generated lookup code was changed from iterating with `i <= bioscfg_drv.type##_instances_count` to `i < bioscfg_drv.type##_instances_count`, and the string comparison condition was extended to first check that `bioscfg_drv.type##_data[i].attr_name_kobj` is non-NULL before accessing its `name` field.

It iterates with `for (i = 0; i <= bioscfg_drv.type##_instances_count; i++)`, which goes one past the valid last element if `type##_instances_count` is the number of instances. Inside that loop it dereferences `bioscfg_drv.type##_data[i].attr_name_kobj->name` in `strcmp(...)` with no check that `attr_name_kobj` is non-NULL.
